lesson.title: Explanation
lesson.summary: Traces object construction and method dispatch to show how field access and method calls resolve differently based on reference type versus runtime type.
lesson.note: Fields and static methods use the reference type (compile-time type) to decide which version is accessed, while instance methods use the actual object's class (runtime type) to decide which version runs.
steps: new B() triggers B's constructor, which calls super() to run A's constructor. Before A's constructor body executes, A's field initializers set s = "A" and n = 1. Then A's constructor calls show(). Because the actual object is B, B's show() is dispatched. But B's own field initializers have not run yet, so B's s is null and B's n is 0. super.s is "A" and super.n is 1. The expression null + 0 + "A" + 1 + " " produces the string "null0A1 ", which is printed.

Back in A's constructor, n += 10 makes A's n equal 11. After super() returns, B's field initializers and instance initializer block run in source order: s becomes "B", n becomes 2, then the block { n *= 3 } makes n equal 6.

B's constructor body continues: show() is called again, dispatching to B's show(). Now B's fields are set, so s is "B", n is 6, super.s is "A", and super.n is 11. The expression "B" + 6 + "A" + 11 + " " prints "B6A11 ". Then n += 100 makes B's n equal 106.
In main, x.show() dispatches to B's show() (runtime type is B), printing "B106A11 ".

The println expression: x.s uses A's field ("A"), x.n uses A's field (11), ((B) x).s uses B's field ("B"), ((B) x).n uses B's field (106), x.who() is a static method resolved by reference type A ("a"), and ((A) null).who() is a static method resolved by reference type A ("a"). Concatenated: "A" + 11 + "B" + 106 + "a" + "a" gives "A11B106aa", and println adds a newline.

concepts.explanation: A method that is re-declared in a subclass with the same signature. When called on an object, the version from the object's actual class runs, not the version matching the reference type.

When a subclass constructor calls super(), the superclass constructor runs first. After super() returns, the subclass's own field initializers and instance initializer blocks run in source order, before the rest of the subclass constructor body.
A class declared static inside another class. It does not need an instance of the enclosing class. It is nested, but is not a non-static inner class.
